newsitem.title: USA: Fed Chairman Greenspan meets U.S. Senate leader.
newsitem.headline: Fed Chairman Greenspan meets U.S. Senate leader.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan met with Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott Thursday.
Greenspan was in Lott's office for about 45 minutes and left without any comment to waiting reporters.
A spokeswoman for Lott, a Republican from Mississippi, would only say that Lott's schedule Thursday was not public.
A Fed spokesman confirmed that the meeting took place but would not comment further.
Lott on Sunday said he was a little nervous about the Fed and the independence it enjoys.
"I'm a little nervous about the degree of independence they have, but at the same time I realize that's very important," the Republican leader told Fox television.
Lott's comments came after Greenspan shook global world financial markets last week by alluding to the economic dangers posed when "irrational exuberance" infects prices.
"They make mistakes like we do," Lott said, when asked about Greenspan's remarks. "I think probably the chairman would say, 'I wish I had chosen some other words'."
